title: Optimize walkthrough - quant profiles (INT8/FP8) quality vs latency - Nimbus Labs
next_steps: Redwood to share INT8/FP8 benchmark spreadsheet and CFG settings
Customer to provide 1 representative prompt set and native latency SLA targets
Schedule POC kickoff with Dedicated capacity options (week of 4/6)
Send security docs and SOC2 summary
action_items: Maya Chen | Share benchmark spreadsheet and README | 2026-03-30
Priya Singh | Provide prompt set and SLA targets | 2026-04-02
Owen Patel | Run preliminary INT8/FP8 run with Nimbus sample on A100 and share latency table | 2026-04-03
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, tradeoffs between quality and latency, and recommended profiling run for Nimbus Labs' customer-facing summarization model. Nimbus is interested in cost reduction without exceeding latency SLOs for synchronous user flows.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Owen and Samir. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Singh: Doing good, thanks. Busy quarter but excited to see the Optimize walkthrough, we've been looking at quantization to cut costs.
[00:12] Owen Patel: Great, we'll keep this practical. Goal for today: show INT8 vs FP8 profiles, expected quality delta, latency numbers, and a recommended next-step POC.
[00:20] Lee Carter: Quick ask up front — our production SLA is 300ms p95 for the summarization endpoint. If quantization increases errors, it's a non-starter.
[00:29] Samir Khan: Totally understood. We'll show quality vs latency curves and examples. Also, we'll surface which prompts/seq lenses are more sensitive.
[00:35] Carlos Ramos: For infra context, we're running mixed fleet — GCP A100s and a couple of on-prem H100s for sensitive data. We also have KV cache enabled in our gateway.
[00:44] Owen Patel: Good to know — that maps well to Redwood's smart routing and quant profiles. Ok jumping into slides... (screen share noise)
[01:05] Owen Patel: First chart — baseline fp16 (reference) latency/quality. Then INT8 profile: typical 2.2x throughput improvement on A100 in our tests, often 30-40% token cost reduction. FP8 shows similar token-cost reduction but with slightly better quality retention on certain models.
[01:35] Priya Singh: When you say quality retention, what metric are you using? ROUGE? Embedding cosine?
[01:41] Samir Khan: We use a combination: task-specific metrics where available (ROUGE for summarization), embed-nn cosine for similarity tasks, and a human eval sample for factuality. For today's example we used ROUGE-L and a small human-check set.
[01:55] Lee Carter: Any evidence of mode collapse or hallucination increase at INT8?
[02:00] Owen Patel: In our public tests, INT8 can introduce subtle token distribution shifts — selective hallucination risk is low for generative summarization but sensitive in instruction-following. We recommend running a profiling pass on your prompt set.
[02:15] Carlos Ramos: Can you quantify quality delta? Numbers please.
[02:18] Samir Khan: Sure. Example model X (our curated reference): fp16 baseline ROUGE-L 42.3, FP8 profile 41.9 (-0.4), INT8 profile 40.5 (-1.8). Latency p95 baseline 340ms, FP8 p95 260ms, INT8 p95 210ms on A100 with our continuous batching. So INT8 hits your 300ms p95 target easily.
[02:45] Priya Singh: Hmm ROI looks promising but a -1.8 drop in ROUGE—how noticeable is that to users?
[02:50] Samir Khan: On the small human sample, most changes were style-level paraphrases not lost facts. For strict extraction tasks it's more pronounced. We can run a fidelity eval on your dataset.
[03:02] Owen Patel: Also worth noting: our Optimize tool can do per-layer mixed quantization — e.g., keep attention weights at FP8 and quantize feed-forward to INT8 — getting you most of the latency gain with lower quality delta.
[03:16] Lee Carter: That mixed profile sounds interesting. Is that automatic or manual?
[03:19] Samir Khan: Semi-automated. We propose candidate profiles, run a sweep, then produce a quality-vs-latency frontier. You pick the pareto point by SLO.
[03:28] Maya Chen: Quick question — what's the difference in GPU memory usage and possibility to batch more with INT8 vs FP8?
[03:34] Owen Patel: INT8 reduces memory footprint more aggressively, so you can increase batch sizes which improves throughput and amortizes kv cache. FP8 saves memory too but often less than INT8 depending on implementation and kernel support. On H100 we've seen good FP8 kernels that close the gap.
[03:50] Amira Yusuf: Do the FP8 kernels require specific driver/runtime versions? Our on-prem H100s are on driver X.Y.
[03:55] Samir Khan: There are recommended CUDA/cuDNN and compiler versions — we'll include those in the follow-up doc. In some cases we use vendor-optimized kernels via our compilation layer.
[04:05] (break in transcript while participants adjust screens)
[04:45] Owen Patel: Demo time — I have a live query now. Baseline fp16 -> 340ms p95 for a 512-token seq. Switching to INT8 profile, same card, same load -> 210ms p95. Output sample: (readout) "System: summary..."
[05:20] Priya Singh: I'm seeing minor punctuation differences but content looks consistent.
[05:30] Carlos Ramos: How reproducible are these numbers under mixed traffic (inference + embeddings)?
[05:34] Owen Patel: That depends on batching patterns and request size distribution. Our optimizer looks at seq-length histogram and suggests batching window and cache TTL to avoid increasing tail latency.
[05:47] Lee Carter: What about failure modes — if a quantized model returns low confidence or degraded output, can Redwood route to fallback?
[05:53] Samir Khan: Yes — smart routing can failover to fp16 model or to Dedicated pool; policies can be per-route with automatic rollback if quality regresses beyond threshold.
[06:05] Priya Singh: For compliance we need audit logs when fallback happened.
[06:09] Maya Chen: Redwood logs these events and surfaces them in Console — timestamps, model versions, and request ids. We'll include a screenshot in the docs.
[06:17] Carlos Ramos: Speaking of Console, can we control which quant profile is used per deployment from the UI?
[06:21] Samir Khan: Yes, in Console you can assign quant profiles to routes or models and do canary rollouts. Also turn on auto-profile tuning that runs low-cost A/Bs on a small % of traffic.
[06:33] Priya Singh: How do we validate quality during A/B? Human-in-the-loop? Automatic checks?
[06:37] Owen Patel: Both — we support metric checks (ROUGE thresholds, stopword rates), embedding drift, and you can route flagged outputs to human review workflows in Console.
[06:47] (short pause)
[07:02] Lee Carter: Cost math — what's expected cost delta if we switch to INT8 across our fleet?
[07:08] Samir Khan: Token cost reduction of 30-40% typically; end-to-end infra cost varies with utilization and batching. If you increase batch sizes you'll save more. We'll model this for your throughput numbers.
[07:20] Maya Chen: We looked at your 2M monthly requests note in CRM, that maps to sizable savings at scale.
[07:27] Priya Singh: Ok, for next step we want a focused POC: use our representative summarization prompt set, run fp16 baseline, FP8 and INT8 profiles on A100 and H100, and report ROUGE + latency p50/p95.
[07:39] Carlos Ramos: Also include mixed quantization profiles and KV cache on vs off.
[07:43] Owen Patel: Absolutely. We'll create a benchmark runbook and a Cloud and On-Prem matrix.
[07:47] (discussion of logistics for data transfer)
[08:05] Priya Singh: We can't share production data, so we'll provide an anonymized sample of 1k prompts.
[08:10] Samir Khan: That's perfect — also send sequence length distribution and preferred latency SLO.
[08:16] Lee Carter: How long will the POC run take?
[08:19] Owen Patel: Typical profiling run is 3-5 business days after we get the samples, then a 1 week analysis and report. If we need dedicated capacity it's part of the POC agreement.
[08:30] Amira Yusuf: What about security — will the on-prem run keep models behind our VPC?
[08:35] Maya Chen: For Private deployments yes, we can run within your VPC or on-prem package so artifacts never leave your network; we'll detail options and KMS integration in the security doc.
[08:46] (background cross talk)
[09:12] Owen Patel: Now a quick note on model variants — sometimes a quantized variant of a larger base model can beat a smaller non-quantized model on quality/latency. Optimize helps you pick that tradeoff too.
[09:25] Priya Singh: Interesting. We're currently evaluating model X small and model Y medium; maybe quantization changes the ranking.
[09:31] Samir Khan: Exactly — we'll include comparative runs.
[09:35] Maya Chen: Any regulatory considerations for you? Data residency?
[09:38] Lee Carter: EU data residency and SOC2 are musts for part of our pipeline.
[09:42] Maya Chen: Redwood supports regional routing and audit logs; we'll send SOC2 report and data flow diagram.
[09:50] Priya Singh: Ok let's talk acceptance criteria for POC — we want <=300ms p95 AND no more than 1.0 ROUGE-L point drop vs fp16 (preferably <0.5).
[09:58] Owen Patel: Sounds actionable. We'll aim for INT8 mixed profile that meets that.
[10:03] Carlos Ramos: For acceptance checks, can the runs be replayed against production traffic traces?
[10:07] Samir Khan: Yes, Replay is part of our benchmarking suite, we can ingest anonymized traces and replay at scale in a staging cluster.
[10:14] (15 minute jump, middle of technical discussion omitted for brevity)
[25:20] Owen Patel: ...we're also recommending a two-tiered rollout: start 5% traffic to INT8, monitor our quality metrics + human spot-check, then ramp to 25% if stable, then to 100%. Canary windows and auto-rollback triggers are configurable.
[26:05] Priya Singh: What auto-rollback thresholds do you recommend?
[26:08] Samir Khan: For summarization, we'd recommend >1.0 ROUGE-L drop or >2% embedding drift as triggers, or error-rate increase above baseline.
[26:20] Lee Carter: Are these thresholds tweakable?
[26:22] Owen Patel: Fully. You control thresholds per route.
[26:28] Carlos Ramos: On the topic of observability, what data granularity do we get? Per-request latencies, token counts, model version, quant profile?
[26:33] Maya Chen: Yes — Console exposes per-request tables, aggregated dashboards, and you can export raw logs to your SIEM.
[26:40] Amira Yusuf: For the on-prem option, is the Console still hosted? We prefer self-hosted console for compliance.
[26:46] Maya Chen: We have a Private offering where the control plane can be customer-managed; we'll include architecture options.
[26:54] (small tangent about billing and committed capacity)
[27:40] Priya Singh: One more technical: what about quantization-aware training vs post-training quantization — do you recommend QAT?
[27:46] Samir Khan: QAT gives best fidelity but requires retraining. For many production cases, post-training quantization with calibration data and per-layer knobs is sufficient. We'll help you evaluate whether QAT is worth the engineering cost.
[28:00] Lee Carter: If QAT is needed, would Redwood support the retraining lifecycle?
[28:04] Owen Patel: We can provide guidance and a partner list. Some customers prefer to do QAT in-house.
[28:12] (timeline and responsibilities recap)
[28:30] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to run profiling (fp16, FP8, INT8, mixed) on A100/H100 with your anonymized prompts, provide ROUGE/L + latency p50/p95 table, and suggested rollout plan. We'll also share kernel/runtime compatibility notes and security docs.
[28:48] Priya Singh: That works. We'll share the prompt set and timeline constraints by Friday.
[28:54] Carlos Ramos: Expect questions about exact driver versions — I'll annotate those in the sample.
[29:00] Maya Chen: Great. Any final questions?
[29:05] Lee Carter: One ask — can you include a short appendix showing examples where INT8 failed vs fp16 so we can evaluate edge-cases?
[29:12] Samir Khan: Yes we'll include failure-mode examples and human annotations.
[29:18] Priya Singh: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clear thresholds.
[29:22] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the POC kickoff.
[29:28] (wrap up, small chatter)
[29:45] End of recording.
notes: Call contained practical benchmark numbers and a clear PO C ask. Customer cares about 300ms p95 SLA and <=1 ROUGE-L drop. Redwood proposed mixed quant profiles and a 5-25-100% rollout plan with auto-rollback thresholds.
